brief: Gold fell 9% over Nov 17-20 (10% on the week), breaking below $3,600 for the first time since September 2025, as a Nasdaq selloff tied to the Anthropic IPO aftermath became the worst equity session since Liberation Day. Goldman's Robert Quinn argues the equity drawdown, not the dollar or real rates, was the catalyst: speculators sold gold to raise cash, a margin-call dynamic Goldman's Thomas and Struyven had already flagged as a 2027 outlook risk from AI-cycle uncertainty. In an earlier Nov 10-17 leg, a hot CPI print and hawkish Fedspeak drove a $9.3bn speculative gold selloff (two-thirds long liquidation, one-third new shorts), cutting net spec length to about $72bn from a $130bn September peak. By Nov 20, gold's 3-month 25-delta put-call skew and implied volatility had both moved 4-5 standard deviations, with skew at a multiyear high. Quinn notes such skew spikes have reverted about 70% of the time within a week since late 2022, implying near-term relief is likely but not necessarily a bottom if Nasdaq-driven margin calls keep coming. ANZ sees scope for further liquidation despite roughly 200 tonnes already sold.
